newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti -- puzzle over PC buyer and rights.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti -- puzzle over PC buyer and rights.

text.p: Analysts puzzled over the identity of a buyer for Olivetti's ailing personal computers on Friday with most bets on a Far East purchaser emerging, but the thought of another rights issue filled them with horror.

Olivetti's new chief executive Roberto Colaninno told the industrial commission of Italy's Senate (upper house) on Thursday that the group thought it had found a buyer for its PCs and said a capital increase may be needed at the end of 1997.

After two failled alliances with U.S. computer giants AT&T and Digital in recent years and most U.S. groups aleady present in Europe, analysts focused the possibility of a Far East purchaser for the PC division.
But the logic of a low-cost producer there wanting a European site perplexed them.

"The favourite option would be for a Far Eastern producer wishing to enter the European market and get hold of Olivetti's customer base. But the logic of a move has to be questioned," said one London-based industry analyst.
Earlier this week, Japanese giants NEC and Sony denied interest in Olivetti's PC company, which lost 200 billion lire ($130 million) in 1995 and in the first half of 1996 was 10 billion in the red.
A source at Olivetti said that an agreement on the future of the PC company was likely to be signed in "weeks rather than days", but he did not add any further details.

One analyst suggested a possible buyer might be the Taiwan private firm Chaplet which makes all Olivetti's lap-top computers under Olivetti's design. Colaninno on Thursday appeared to suggest the buyer would come from one of Olivetti's existing suppliers.
However, the Olivetti source suggested the Taiwanese option was wide of the mark.

Many analysts did not believe that the PC company was worth anything to sell, but for Olivetti a sale for a nominal amount would be preferable to the cost and political outcry that would follow a move to close the company down.
Analysts estimate it could cost 400-500 billion lire for closure while the loss of 1,750 jobs in Olivetti home town of Ivrea in north-western Italy could produce a political backlash.
Of further concern to analysts was talk of another rights issue after the group made a massive 2.26 trillion lire rescue rights issue at the end of last year.
"The rights issue then was for a huge amount, was soon absorbed, the share price halved and now the company wants more," said the London analyst.

Colaninno has said he plans to raise 800 billion lire from asset sales this year and raise a further 400 billion in 1997. According to analysts these asset sales are needed for the payment of 1.2 trillion lire of loans as they fall due.

"The assumption is that the banks are unwilling to roll over these term loans, and that Olivetti needs to pay them off. But this leaves them with no money to invest in its growing telecoms businesses," said an analyst with an Italian bank.

The asset sales have not been specified but will include the PC company, a 5.6 percent stake in mobile phone consortium Omnitel, the sale of speciality computer systems unit Tecnost and a flotation of office equipment company Lexikon in 1997.
"Olivetti is now following a path which could result in the group's long term survival, but it may be too late," said the Italian bank analyst. ($1=1,522 lire)
